title: Firefox on Linux randomly stops loading all pages after repeated network changes
body: I use Firefox 125 on Linux for a long time, and at random its networking stalls so I cannot open any page. Chrome can still open the same page, and restarting Firefox makes it work again. I do not know what triggers it. I captured profiles with the Networking and HTTP/3 presets. I think this only happens on Linux; I have not encountered it on Windows.

symptoms_visible: After Firefox has been running for a long time on Linux, networking randomly stalls and I cannot open any page.
Chrome can still open the same page, and restarting Firefox makes Firefox work normally again.
N0.label: N0 random Linux networking stall reported

symptoms_visible: The same all-pages stall occurs in Troubleshooting Mode even though I have no extensions installed.
On one occurrence, pages started working again after around ten minutes without restarting Firefox.
N1.label: N1 extension theory excluded

symptoms_visible: The networking stall still occurs after setting Firefox to No proxy.
When it happens, every tested page remains pending while other applications still have connectivity.
N2.label: N2 no-proxy stall with complex network environment

symptoms_visible: With network.http.max-connections reduced, I did not encounter the random stall during a one-hour test, but the setting made normal browsing difficult.
N2_x.label: N2_x reduced connection-limit probe

symptoms_visible: A failed Docker container was restarting repeatedly, and Firefox logged a network change about once per minute.
After disconnecting the main Wi-Fi interface and refreshing about:networking, some socket entries remain listed.
N3.label: N3 repeated network changes and retained sockets observed

symptoms_visible: Even after stopping Docker and bringing all network interfaces down, about:networking still lists some IP socket entries.
Opening cloudflare.com, disconnecting Wi-Fi, and refreshing the page reproduces socket entries remaining in about:networking.
N4.label: N4 retained sockets reproduced with interfaces down

symptoms_visible: On a fresh Linux Mint virtual machine, a socket remains listed after opening cloudflare.com and disconnecting the internet.
With network.http.http2.move_to_pending_list_after_network_change set to false, the remaining connection disappears after waiting about 60 seconds.
N5.label: N5 regression and pending-list behavior isolated

symptoms_visible: After updating to a build containing the networking fix, pending connections close after the network changes and Firefox continues loading pages without requiring a restart.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Can you run Firefox in Troubleshooting Mode and report whether the stall still occurs?
Please test whether the issue reproduces with extensions and hardware acceleration temporarily disabled.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. It took a while because it happens randomly, but I confirmed the issue still occurs in Troubleshooting Mode.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I can only reproduce it in normal mode; it never occurs in Troubleshooting Mode, and disabling my extensions prevents it.
It also occurs in Troubleshooting Mode, but it took several days instead of two weeks to happen.

edges.comment: Comments 2-4: Troubleshooting Mode was a handler-initiated configuration probe, so it is represented as a clarification. The reporter also volunteered that no extensions were installed, that one stall recovered after about ten minutes, and that a full log became too large to upload.

question_patterns: Does the issue still happen if Firefox is set to No proxy rather than Use system proxy settings?
Please disable proxy use, restart if necessary, and report whether the networking stall returns.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The problem still happened after I changed the setting to No proxy.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No. After switching to No proxy and restarting Firefox, the stall never returned under the same office usage.

question_patterns: What is the current value of network.http.max-connections?
Can you check network.http.max-connections in about:config?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: network.http.max-connections is set to 900, which I think is the default.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It was manually set to 10; restoring the default prevents the stall.
It is 900 and has never been modified.

question_patterns: Can you capture an HTTP log while Firefox is stalled and share the file?
Please save a networking log covering an occurrence rather than only a profiler capture.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I captured and attached a log from an occurrence. A few minutes of logging was already around 400 MB, so recording from browser startup for more than four hours is not practical.

edges.comment: Comments 5-10: the proxy toggle was a measurement even though the changed setting was retained. The reporter also volunteered the office machine's many interfaces, Docker networks, and Wi-Fi switching script.

question_patterns: Can you temporarily reduce network.http.max-connections and see whether that makes the problem reproduce more easily?
Please test with a small maximum connection count and capture a log if the stall appears.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested a reduced value for about one hour and did not reproduce the issue. It also made Firefox too hard to use normally.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With the limit set to 10, I can reproduce the same permanent stall within minutes every time.

edges.comment: Comments 11-13: reducing the limit was a diagnostic measurement, not the fix. The raw outcome does not establish whether connections are leaking.

question_patterns: After a network change or Wi-Fi disconnect, what remains in about:networking#sockets?
Can you disconnect the main network interface, refresh about:networking, and share what you see?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When I disconnect the main Wi-Fi and refresh about:networking#sockets, some connections are still listed. I also noticed a failed Docker container was restarting and causing a network-change event about every minute, so I stopped that container.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The sockets list clears immediately every time I disconnect Wi-Fi; no entries survive the network change.
The about:networking page uses a different color theme on this machine.

edges.comment: Comment 15: the socket-list screenshot answers the interface-change probe. In the same update, the reporter discovered and stopped a repeatedly restarting Docker container; that retained system change creates state S3.

question_patterns: Are all network interfaces disconnected, including Docker and Ethernet, when those sockets remain?
Please stop Docker, bring all interfaces down, and show whether about:networking still lists addresses.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I first disconnected only the main Wi-Fi while the Docker network was still running. In this test I believe I stopped Docker and brought all interfaces down, but some IP entries were still left.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Once Docker, Ethernet, and Wi-Fi are all down, every socket entry disappears immediately.

question_patterns: Can you capture a short log around a controlled disconnect instead of logging the entire session?
Please open one site, disconnect Wi-Fi, refresh it, and save the resulting HTTP log.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I enabled logging, opened cloudflare.com, disabled Wi-Fi, and refreshed cloudflare.com. I attached the resulting log; there may have been another step that I forgot.

edges.comment: Comments 16-18: the reporter clarified that the first test left Docker active, then supplied a second screenshot with interfaces down and a short controlled-disconnect log.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce the retained socket on a clean Linux installation?
Does a fresh Linux virtual machine show the same connection remaining after an internet disconnect?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. On a fresh Linux Mint install in VirtualBox, I opened cloudflare.com, disconnected the internet, and about:networking still showed a socket.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: A clean Linux installation always clears the socket; I can reproduce it only on the office machine with its Docker setup.
The same clean-system reproduction works on a physical Linux machine instead of VirtualBox.

question_patterns: Can you run mozregression on the short disconnect reproduction and share its raw result?
Please bisect the retained-socket behavior between a working and failing Firefox build.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran mozregression, and it said the bug came from Bug 1706377.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Mozregression places the change before Bug 1706377 and gives a range containing only unrelated DNS work.

question_patterns: Can you set network.http.http2.move_to_pending_list_after_network_change to false and repeat the disconnect test?
Please toggle the HTTP/2 move-to-pending-list preference in a test profile and report how long the remaining socket lasts.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With network.http.http2.move_to_pending_list_after_network_change set to false, about:networking initially still shows a connection, but after about 60 seconds no connection is left.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The socket remains indefinitely with the preference either true or false.

edges.comment: Comment 19: the reporter independently produced a clean Linux reproduction, a mozregression result naming Bug 1706377, and a preference-toggle result. These are raw user-produced measurements; the missing DontReuse mechanism belongs to the final engineer inference.

solution.intent: Fix the regression in the HTTP connection manager by marking connections moved to the pending list after a network change as non-reusable, allowing them to close after their final transaction instead of accumulating toward the global connection limit.
solution.concrete_example: When a network change moves an HTTP/2 connection to the pending list, call DontReuse() on it. The connection will then close after its last transaction completes rather than remaining reusable and accumulating across repeated network changes. Please retest in today's build and confirm that sockets clear and pages continue loading after repeated disconnects.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter's measurements establish that sockets survive Linux network changes, mozregression names Bug 1706377, and disabling network.http.http2.move_to_pending_list_after_network_change lets the connection disappear. Engineers inferred the precise mechanism: connections moved to the pending list were not marked non-reusable, so frequent network-change events could accumulate them until Firefox reached its global connection limit. The patch calls DontReuse(), causing each pending connection to close after its final transaction.

edges.comment: Comments 20-23: the technical fix was to call DontReuse() for pending connections so they close after the last transaction. Uplift and release-management comments are intentionally not scored.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause as the Bug 1706377 regression in network-change handling: HTTP/2 connections moved to the pending list remained reusable and could accumulate across frequent network changes until Firefox reached its connection limit.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the retained sockets after interface disconnects, the clean Linux reproduction, the mozregression result, and the move_to_pending_list_after_network_change preference probe.
The fix must mark the pending connections non-reusable with DontReuse() so they close after their final transaction.

Must not settle on extensions, proxy configuration, or permanently reducing network.http.max-connections as the fix; the issue reproduced in Troubleshooting Mode, with No proxy, and a reduced limit did not provide a usable resolution.
Must ask the reporter to verify on a build containing the fix that sockets close after network changes and normal page loading continues before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Linux user who can capture HTTP logs and profiler traces, inspect about:networking, manage interfaces and Docker, use VirtualBox, edit about:config preferences, and run mozregression.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and experimental, with concise informal English; reports uncertainty explicitly, supplies detailed environment observations, and independently develops smaller reproduction steps.
